steps.instruction:
Requirement: the watchlist must display movies the user has not watched yet BEFORE movies already watched.

Implement this entirely inside the watchlist component:

1. Make `movies` a computed signal derived from `store.items()`. It must return every item, with all unwatched items (`watched === false`) first, followed by all watched items (`watched === true`). Within each group, preserve the store's current relative order (stable sort on a copy, e.g. `[...this.store.items()].sort((a, b) => Number(a.watched) - Number(b.watched))`). Do NOT mutate or reorder the store's underlying items or its persisted order.
2. The template must render the list from `movies()`. If it currently iterates `store.items()` (or any other unsorted source) directly, switch it to `movies()`, so the visible on-screen order is unwatched-first. All other behaviour (row click, toggle, remove, counts/progress, announcement) stays as is; counts should still come from the store's own signals, not from the sorted list.
3. Exported signatures stay unchanged: `movies` remains `Signal<WatchItem[]>`; `store`, `watchedCount`, `progress`, `announcement`, `toggleWatched`, `onRowClick`, `remove` keep their current declarations. Do not modify WatchlistStore or any other unit.

If an existing test in your spec file asserts the previous insertion order of the rendered list, do not edit it silently - submit it as a test-change request explaining that it conflicts with this new ordering requirement.

testChangeReasons.reason: This test depended on the previous rendered order: after clicking the first row's checkbox it re-queried items()[0]'s checkbox via checkbox(), which only pointed at the same checkbox because a toggled movie used to stay in place. With the required unwatched-first ordering, the movie that becomes watched re-renders at the end of the list, so the index-based re-query now finds the other (still unchecked) checkbox and the assertion fails. The edit holds a reference to the clicked checkbox before the click, preserving the test's intent (clicking a checkbox toggles that movie); all other assertions are unchanged and the test still passes under the old ordering too.
testChangeReasons.title: Watchlist > toggles watched when the checkbox is clicked

testChangeReasons.reason: Same conflict with the new ordering requirement: clicking blank space on the first row makes that movie watched, so the row moves to the bottom of the rendered list; the original assertion checkbox() re-queried whatever is now first, which would be the other movie's unchecked checkbox and fail. The edit keeps a reference to the clicked row and asserts on the checkbox inside it, preserving the test's intent that clicking blank space on a row toggles that row's movie.
